## Findings
- claim-1: The paper formally conjectures that both Schur-function generating sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}, \] for \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), are minimal; each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1380-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The stronger unresolved statement is \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}, \] and the authors explicitly state that a proof had eluded them. [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Let \(M\) be a bounded-below graded module over a connected graded ring \(\Lambda\), and let \(G\) be either homogeneous family above. If the image of \(G\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(M/\Lambda_+M\), then \(G\) is a minimal \(\Lambda\)-generating family. Indeed, the source’s graded Nakayama proposition identifies generation and inclusion-minimality with spanning and minimal spanning in \(M/\Lambda_+M\); a basis is minimally spanning. [source-2@L1520-L1534|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: A rational rank calculation cannot prove the stronger statement or minimality integrally: \(2\in\mathbb Z\) is a basis after tensoring with \(\mathbb Q\), but does not generate \(\mathbb Z\); and \(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\) has a minimal one-element generating set but is not free. Thus a direct proof must exclude both nonunit indices and torsion.
- claim-5: The directory reports a separate open question: determine minimal generating sets for general type-\(A\) ideals \(I_w\); the cited primary-source passage is not supplied here, so this identification is not independently primary-source verified. [source-6@L88-L102|claim=ordinary-document]
## Strategy
Let \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) and \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\). The source-backed theorem supplies either proposed \(N\)-element family \(G\) as a generating family for \(J_v\); hence
\[
\mathbb Z^{N}\twoheadrightarrow Q,\qquad e_\mu\mapsto \overline{s_\mu}.
\]

A direct proof should establish the all-degree rational statement
\[
\dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q\otimes\mathbb Q)=N,
\]
preferably degreewise, with Hilbert series equal to the degree distribution of the proposed interval family:
\[
\sum_{\mu}t^{|\mu|}=t^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_t.
\]
This requires a complete rational presentation of every graded piece of \(Q\): Schur columns for \(J_v\) and all positive-degree Pieri-product rows generating \((\Lambda_+J_v)_d\). One may then prove the claimed Hilbert series by a uniform elimination, a dual family of functionals annihilating all Pieri rows, or a standard-monomial/Gröbner argument.

Once the rational dimension is proved, no separate Smith-form or torsion argument is needed. If \(K\) is the kernel of \(\mathbb Z^N\twoheadrightarrow Q\), then
\[
K\otimes\mathbb Q=0
\]
because \(Q\otimes\mathbb Q\) has dimension \(N\). Since \(K\subseteq\mathbb Z^N\) is torsion-free, this implies \(K=0\). Therefore
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z^N,
\]
and the images of the specified proposed generators are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. Graded Nakayama then gives their inclusion-minimality.

## Gaps
The necessary all-degree rational-dimension proof is not supplied. Existing accepted calculations cover only specified boundary regimes and bounded degrees; they do not establish the required Hilbert series or rational independence generally.

The source records minimality as a conjecture and reports that a proof had eluded the authors at publication; it does not establish current unresolved status.

Finite Smith-form computations, if later supplied, would be evidence only for their tested parameters and must track the proposed generator coordinates explicitly.

## Next
Prove a uniform all-degree Schur/Pieri presentation for \(Q\otimes\mathbb Q\), then derive its graded Hilbert series \(t^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_t\). Apply the integral surjective-kernel argument above to obtain freeness and minimality.
